\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انفجار} (enfejâr)}{انفجار (enfejâr)}]{\fa{انفجار} (enfejâr) — an explosion}

\label{lesson:FA-C329-enfejar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for smoke, then the Persian for a spark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انفجار}}
\textbf{\fa{انفجار}} (\emph{enfejâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}an explosion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صدای} \fa{انفجار} \fa{همه} \fa{را} \fa{بیدار} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sedâ-ye enfejâr hame râ bidâr kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sound of the explosion woke everyone up.
\end{quote}

\emph{Enfejâr-e gâz} \textquotedblleft{}a gas explosion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{enfejâr} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{infijār}, \textquotedblleft{}explosion, bursting\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists both the Arabic and the Persian word).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{enfejâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{enfejâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{enfejâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for smoke, then the Persian for a spark, then say \emph{enfejâr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{انفجار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An explosion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{منفجر} \fa{شدن} (monfajer shodan)}{منفجر شدن (monfajer shodan)}]{\fa{منفجر} \fa{شدن} (monfajer shodan) — to explode, to blow up}

\label{lesson:FA-C329-monfajer-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a spark, then the Persian for an explosion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{منفجر} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{منفجر} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{monfajer shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to explode, to blow up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کپسول} \fa{گاز} \fa{در} \fa{آشپزخانه} \fa{منفجر} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kapsul-e gâz dar âshpazkhâne monfajer shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gas cylinder exploded in the kitchen.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{monfajer mishavad}; \emph{monfajer kardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to blow something up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{monfajer} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{munfajir}, \textquotedblleft{}bursting\textquotedblright{}, of the same root as \emph{enfejâr}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a spark, then the Persian for an explosion, then say \emph{monfajer shodan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ترکیدن} (tarakidan)}{ترکیدن (tarakidan)}]{\fa{ترکیدن} (tarakidan) — to burst, to crack}

\label{lesson:FA-C329-tarakidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an explosion, then the Persian for to explode.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ترکیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{ترکیدن}} (\emph{tarakidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to burst, to crack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{لوله} \fa{آب} \fa{در} \fa{زمستان} \fa{ترکید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Lule-ye âb dar zemestân tarakid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The water pipe burst in the winter.
\end{quote}

Spoken \emph{terekidan}. Present stem \emph{tarak-}: \emph{mitarakad}, in speech \emph{mitereke}. Also of a balloon or a tyre.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tarakidan} is a native Persian verb, built with the verb suffix \emph{-idan}; its deeper origin is not settled, and EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarakidan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tarakidan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an explosion, then the Persian for to explode, then say \emph{tarakidan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نشت} \fa{کردن} (nasht kardan)}{نشت کردن (nasht kardan)}]{\fa{نشت} \fa{کردن} (nasht kardan) — to leak}

\label{lesson:FA-C329-nasht-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to explode, then the Persian for to burst.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نشت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{نشت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{nasht kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to leak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گاز} \fa{از} \fa{لوله} \fa{نشت} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gâz az lule nasht mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Gas was leaking from the pipe.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{nasht mikonad}. The noun \emph{nasht} is \textquotedblleft{}a leak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nasht} \textquotedblleft{}a leak, seepage\textquotedblright{} is a native word whose origin is not settled; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خاکستر} (khâkestar)}{خاکستر (khâkestar)}]{\fa{خاکستر} (khâkestar) — ash, ashes}

\label{lesson:FA-C329-khakestar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to burst, then the Persian for to leak.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خاکستر}}
\textbf{\fa{خاکستر}} (\emph{khâkestar}) — \textquotedblleft{}ash, ashes\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{خانه} \fa{فقط} \fa{خاکستر} \fa{ماند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az khâne faqat khâkestar mând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Only ashes were left of the house.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâk} \textquotedblleft{}earth, dust\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-estar}. \emph{Zir-e khâkestar} \textquotedblleft{}under the ashes\textquotedblright{}, smouldering.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâkestar} is built on \emph{khâk} \textquotedblleft{}dust, earth\textquotedblright{}, a native Persian word; EtymDB lists no entry for the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
